title: org.ligatureprotocol.device
description: DRAFT. A device principal or a user-device binding, with the role signatures that make it trusted. Carried by the device itself and gossiped between devices; there is no shared repository. Capabilities are not part of this record: they are announced live in a capability manifest (spec chapters 02, 05, 06). The domain ligatureprotocol.org is a placeholder; it is not yet registered.

publicKey.description: A public key as a multibase string with a multicodec prefix (an Ed25519 key renders as z6Mk…).

roleSignature.description: A signature made in the pairing ceremony. Spec chapter 02 section 3.

role.description: binding: my account on this device; principal: a device I use; person: another master key I know.

signer.description: The master key of the person whose self-signing or user-signing key made the signature.

signature.description: Signature over the signed key and role.

revocation.description: A gossiped statement that a key is no longer trusted. Spec chapters 02 and 07.

subject.description: The revoked key: a binding, a principal, a known person, or an abandoned master key.

signer.description: The master key on whose behalf an introducer signed.

deviceId.description: Stable opaque identifier derived from the key.

displayName.description: Human-readable name chosen by the user.

kind.description: The device itself, or one person's account on it. A personal device is one binding plus its principal (spec chapter 10).

registration.description: For a principal: whether the device belongs to a person (owner set is master keys) or to the group (owner set is the group key; listed in the membership document). Chosen at pairing (spec chapter 02 section 6).

key.description: The principal key or binding key.

person.description: For a binding: the master key of the account holder.

principal.description: For a binding: the deviceId of the principal it runs on.

ownerSet.description: For a principal: master keys allowed to administer the device. The first person to pair a binding on an unowned principal is its first owner.

introducer.description: For a binding: whether it holds the self-signing key and may perform the ceremony for others. Chosen at pairing time according to the user's requirements; implementations should default it to false on a group device.

signatures.description: Role signatures by people who trust this key. A binding carries one from its owner; a principal one per person who uses it.

revoked.description: Retained after revocation so the revocation can be gossiped.
